Privacy

Last updated 6 September 2026.

Hexbot is built so that your data stays on your hardware. This policy explains the small amount that this website and Hexbot Connect handle, and the much larger amount they never see.

This website

hexbot.app sets no cookies and collects no personal information. It has no analytics or third-party scripts. The pairing page reads the daemon address from the query string and the pairing code from the URL fragment. Browsers do not send fragments to web servers, and the page does not transmit or store the code.

Hexbot Connect

Connect, the optional service at connect.hexbot.app, brokers your identity and a hostname so that your own devices can reach your own daemon from outside its network. To do that it stores:

  • Your sign-in identity. Sign-in is handled by Clerk, which holds your email address and any sign-in method you choose. Connect keeps only the Clerk user ID that links your account to your daemons.
  • Registered daemons. The name you gave each daemon, its assigned hostname, its Cloudflare tunnel ID, the port it reports, a hash of its service token, and when it was created, last seen, and revoked.
  • Signed-in devices. The device name each app reported when it signed in, a hash of its session token, and when it was created, last used, and revoked.
  • Pending registrations. The short-lived codes shown by hexbot connect while you approve a daemon. They expire within minutes.

Connect uses these records to list your daemons, issue short-lived login grants, keep tunnels pointed at the right port, and let you revoke access. It does not use them for advertising, profiling, or anything else, and it does not sell or share them.

What Connect never receives

Connect never receives your conversations, bot memory, provider keys, files, tool results, or the long-lived device tokens your daemon issues. Chat traffic travels from your device through Cloudflare's edge and the tunnel process on your daemon host, encrypted with TLS. The Connect API is not in that path and cannot read it.

Service providers

Connect runs on Vercel, stores its records in a Neon Postgres database, signs you in with Clerk, and creates tunnels and DNS records with Cloudflare. Each of these processes data on our behalf under its own privacy policy. Cloudflare carries your encrypted chat traffic as part of running the tunnel; the other providers see only the records listed above.

Retention and deletion

Daemon and device records stay while you keep them registered. Revoking a daemon or device marks it revoked and deletes its tunnel. Running hexbot connect disconnect revokes the daemon and removes the credentials on your machine. To delete your account and every record tied to it, email hello@hexbot.app from the address you signed in with, and we will remove it within 30 days.

The desktop app

The app talks only to the daemon you pair with, your chosen model provider, and Connect if you sign in to it. Crash reporting is off by default; if you turn it on in settings, Electron may upload a crash report when the desktop process crashes, as described in Updates. Update checks fetch a small manifest from this site and send nothing about you.

Self-hosting

If you run your own Connect instance, none of the above reaches us. That instance's operator is responsible for its data.

Changes and contact

We may update this policy. The date at the top tells you when, and material changes will be announced on this site. Questions go to hello@hexbot.app.
